Hardware topology [1.5B run, one node, 8× RTX 6000 Ada]

No FSDP, ZeRO or vLLM in the loop: fit() requires exactly one trainer GPU. The driver, TransferQueue, load balancer, manager, dataset and rollout workers are CPU actors. Ray C++ does not set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, so devices are picked explicitly: trainer = local rank, replica i = replica_device_offset (1) + i.

Control plane — Ray C++ actor RPCs (msgpack)
Only KVBatchMeta {partition_id, keys, tags} and small structs move here. Actors find each other by name: rl_bridge_<type>_<id>.

Data plane — Blu-TransferQueue
Tensors are written once and read by key from any actor with its own TQClient. A prompt and all its trajectories share one storage shard.
Groups with a learning signal (not all-same reward)

Gotchas
• Use the new-ABI venv's ray binary — the bare `ray` on PATH silently breaks the actors.
• Run from RL/: code_search_path = cwd, so Ray finds rollout_bridge_worker.so there (it holds every RAY_REMOTE).
• If a token exists, the binary re-execs itself with RAY_AUTH_MODE=token.

Why pretokenized?  C++ has no tokenizer, so prompt_encoding must be pretokenized_ids for rollout. gsm8k_chat.py applies the chat template + a \boxed{} instruction and stores input_ids. max_prompt_length, truncation (error|left|right|middle) and filter_overlong_prompts are enforced only in this mode. The dataset lives in a singleton Ray actor, and get_state/restore_state make the cursor resumable.

ReplayBufferAsync (a verl port) decides which finished groups train next — and which get thrown away

select_oldest
stable sort by birth step
Only metadata moves here. sample() returns keys; the tensors stay in TransferQueue until the trainer reads them. Metric: timing/sample_wait_s.
Four reasons a group is evicted

stale
Finished but too old (drop strategy only): now − birth + 1 > max_off_policy_threshold [2].

dapo
filter_groups on: every trajectory has the same metric (all 0 or all 1) → zero advantage, no gradient.

failed
Any session threw → the group's status is failure.

unsettled
Status says finished but trajectory rows aren't visible yet (a race the report fixed).

Every evicted group is replaced one-for-one by a fresh prompt (verl refills in whole gen_batch_size chunks). Metrics: training/off_policy/evicted_samples*, training/filter_groups/evicted_samples, training/rollout_failure/evicted_samples.

is_stale(birth, now, thr):  (now − birth + 1) > thr

drop — finished stale groups are evicted and refilled.
wait — has_enough() stays false while any pending/running group has now − birth + 1 ≥ thr, so rollouts can't run too far ahead.
max_off_policy_threshold: null turns staleness control off.

Staleness is measured, not corrected: logprob_gap_by_staleness compares old_log_probs with rollout_log_probs in buckets span0 / span1 / span2plus. There is no importance weight for the rollout-vs-trainer policy gap.

Why it matters on GSM8K: only ~18% of groups carried signal on the raw set. data_preprocess/filter_from_rollouts.py drops prompts the model always or never solves, lifting that to 44–53%. dapo_filtered caches its verdict per uid; metric "reward" sums rm_scores, any other metric reads extra_fields.reward_extra_info[metric].
GRPO advantages on the driver, then one fused CUDA kernel for the clipped policy-gradient + KL loss

s_i   = Σ_t rm_scores[i,t]                  // the outcome score
group = key prefix before '_'           // same prompt uid
μ_g  = mean(s over group)
σ_g  = std(s over group, ddof = 1)       // Bessel

GRPO    (norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo = true):  A_i = (s_i − μ_g) / (σ_g + 1e-6)
Dr.GRPO (norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo = false): A_i =  s_i − μ_g

group of size 1 → μ = 0, σ = 1   (verl's special case)
A_i is broadcast to every response token; computed on CPU

Correct answers get +1.62, wrong ones −0.54.
Dr.GRPO gives +0.75 / −0.25 (no ÷ σ), so easy and hard prompts aren't rescaled.
2 · Per-token loss  (GRPOLossKernels.cu — one CUDA block per valid token row)

log πθ    = logit[target] − logsumexp(logits)          // block reduction over the vocab
ratio r   = exp(clamp(log πθ − log π_old, −20, 20))     // 1 if no π_old
unclipped = r · A
clipped   = clip(r, 1 − clip_ratio_low, 1 + clip_ratio_high) · A
objective = min(unclipped, clipped)
if clip_ratio_c > 0 and A < 0:  objective = max(objective, clip_ratio_c · A)   // dual clip

x  = clamp(log π_ref − log πθ, −20, 20)
kl = eˣ − x − 1  ≥ 0                                     // k3 / low_var_kl

loss_i = −objective + kl_loss_coef · kl                   // coef 0.001; 0 if use_kl_loss = false

Gradient routing
The PG gradient flows only when the unclipped branch is the active min and isn't overridden by the dual-clip floor. clipfrac counts the rows where it isn't. The KL gradient dkl/dlog πθ = 1 − eˣ is zeroed once x saturates at ±20.
Not implemented: kl_loss_type other than low_var_kl throws · calculate_entropy=true throws · entropy_coeff is parsed but never read · use_kl_in_reward is unused.
3 · What clip and KL look like
A > 0: objective / A vs ratio r
A = −1: objective vs r (dual clip c = 3)
k3 KL:  eˣ − x − 1,  x = log π_ref − log πθ

Dashed grey = no clipping. Left: for good tokens the gain is capped once r > 1.2. Middle: for bad tokens the loss is capped once r < 0.8, and the dual-clip floor stops it growing past c·A when r explodes. Right: k3 is always ≥ 0, ≈ x²/2 near 0, and an unbiased low-variance KL estimate.
4 · Turning per-token losses into one number (loss_agg_mode)
weight w_i for each valid token
Every token counts the same; long answers weigh more.
Every sequence counts the same (original GRPO).
Sum over tokens, mean over sequences (no length norm).
loss = Σ loss_i · w_i with a deterministic per-row-slot reduction (no atomics), so runs are bit-reproducible. Reported kl and clipfrac are always a plain token mean.

Important consequence
π_old is recomputed by the trainer, with its current weights, right before each optimizer step — and with ppo_epochs = 1 there is one step per batch. So r ≈ 1 at update time, the clip is effectively inactive (actor/pg_clipfrac ≈ 0 in the logs), and the update is a vanilla policy gradient + k3 KL. The rollout-vs-trainer gap from async staleness is not importance-corrected: rollout_log_probs is only used for diagnostics.
TrainerWorker on GPU 0: two models, three RPCs, and the update loop

ProductionGPT = RMSNorm · QK-norm + RoPE (sequential path — the fused kernel ignores strides) · GQA · SwiGLU · tied lm_head (cast before transposing). Sequence length must be a multiple of 64. Allocator SizeClass::set_mode("exact"). Checkpoints load from BluTrain CKPT, .safetensors (param_NNNNNN) or DCPM dirs; convert_hf_qwen3.py converts HF Qwen3.
From the model section of the run YAMLs (production_gqa).
build_batch — the causal-shift frame  (example: P = 4, R = 3)

target[t] = ids[t+1], so the logits at position P−1 … P+R−2 predict the response tokens: mask = 1 exactly there. L = ceil(max(P+R)/64)·64 per micro-batch. scatter_response / gather_response move TQ's [R] vectors into and out of this [b, L] frame.
The three RPCs (keys in, tensors via TQ)

compute_old_log_prob
kv_batch_get(input_ids, prompts) → per micro-batch: build_batch → actor.log_probs_no_grad → gather_response → kv_batch_put(old_log_probs)

compute_ref_log_prob
same, with the reference model → ref_log_prob  (only if loss.use_kl_loss)

update_actor
reads input_ids, prompts, old_log_probs, advantages, rollout_log_probs (+ ref_log_prob) and runs the loop below; returns a metrics map
log_probs_no_grad = NoGradGuard + forward + autograd::grpo_token_logp (fused log-softmax + gather).
for mini-batch of ppo_mini_batch_size × n trajectories  [32 × 8 = 256]   →  zero_grad()
for micro-batch of ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu  [2]   (128 of them)

loss × w  →  backward()
w = tokens_micro / tokens_mini   (token-mean)

One optimizer step per mini-batch; parameter_sync_step [1] mini-batches per global step. Metrics: actor/pg_loss, actor/kl_loss (raw k3 mean, not ×coef), actor/pg_clipfrac, actor/grad_norm, actor/lr, actor/optimizer_steps, framework/rollout_vs_trainer_logprob_{absdiff_mean, diff_mean, absdiff_max, frac_gt1}.

Linear warmup lr·step/warmup, then constant or cosine: min_lr + ½(lr − min_lr)(1 + cos(π·progress)). total = total_steps · parameter_sync_step · ppo_epochs · ceil(groups / mini). warmup = lr_warmup_steps, else ratio × total.
WeightSyncEngine::update_weights — pushing 3.4 GB from GPU 0 to seven replicas in ~0.4 s
keep mode: in-flight requests pause, PagedEngine drops their KV
no-op for both engines (already cleared at pause)
first call only — the group stays warm afterwards
dispatched to everyone before waiting on anyone
paused requests re-prefill under the new weights
Step 5 has no separate call: transfer is steps 4 together. The weight-hash diagnostic (FNV-1a) runs at step ≤ 2 and every 50 — about 4 s per hashed sync.
Buckets: by size and by dtype
parameters in positional order: wte · q k v o projections · norm · gate up down · norm (orange = fp32, blue = bf16)

bucket_by_size(params, MB) starts a new bucket when the size cap [256 MB] is hit or the dtype changes. One dtype per bucket fixed a weight-corruption bug with mixed bf16/fp32. Both sides re-derive the same schedule independently: there are no names on the wire, so trainer ProductionGPT and replica blu::BLU must have identical parameter order and dtypes.

flatten_concat bucket i+1 while bucket i's async broadcast is in flight. A cudaDeviceSynchronize() before every broadcast fixed a race that sent half-written buffers. Replicas: flatten → sync → broadcast (sync) → unflatten_into.

trainer_pool_fsdp — only when there's more than one trainer GPU (and then fit() refuses to run).

weight_sync — trainers are ranks 0…N−1, replicas N…N+M−1 [world 8]. A rejoin with a different rank or world size throws.

Why pause in keep mode instead of aborting? In-flight generations survive the sync: they lose only their KV cache and re-prefill with the new weights, so a sequence can span two policy versions. That's one more source of the off-policy gap the replay buffer's staleness threshold bounds.

AdamW step and 1 weight sync per global step

Invariant: train_batch_size (32) = parameter_sync_step (1) × ppo_mini_batch_size (32), so each step_once() trains on exactly one mini-batch → one optimizer step. With the 135M configs, train_batch_size 8 and parameter_sync_step 2 give two smaller updates per global step.

What gets logged and saved, how runs were evaluated, and what isn't there yet
Quirk: matching is by substring, so …/evicted_samples_staleness/mean contains "evicted" and is summed across mini-batches, not averaged.

actor/*
pg_loss, kl_loss, pg_clipfrac, grad_norm, lr, optimizer_steps

Checkpoints — weights only
<checkpoint.dir>/global_step_<N>/actor.safetensors every save_freq_steps [25] and at the last step. No optimizer state and no rotation; load_checkpoint throws. A continuation run resets AdamW, and its KL reference becomes the continuation checkpoint.

Evaluation is offline
RLDriver::validate() throws and val_path is never used. Instead: scripts/eval_gsm8k_vllm.py scores gsm8k_chat/val.jsonl greedily with vLLM using the same strict rule, and scripts/compare_evals.py runs a paired McNemar test.

Logs
[metrics] {json} lines on stdout + log_dir/metrics.jsonl; per-rollout JSON lines in rollout_data_dir/rollouts_<pid>.jsonl (analyze_rollouts.py, filter_from_rollouts.py read them).

Fixed during the 1.5B bring-up
• NCCL broadcast race → cudaDeviceSynchronize() before each broadcast
• TQ KV_CLEAR freed ids early → Controller::release_cleared()
• "finished" before rows visible → the unsettled set
• mixed-dtype buckets corrupted weights → one dtype per bucket
• step time 73 s → ~35 s

Runs in the repo
135M GPT on GSM8K, 2× RTX 3060 · 1.5B Qwen3-shaped on 8× RTX 6000 Ada (1 trainer + 7 rollout GPUs) · configs: grpo_135m_{gsm8k, sft_gsm8k, oneshot_104, ifeval}, grpo_1p5b_{gsm8k, cont100, 1000, sanity_short}.
Caveats — read before trusting a knob

Single trainer GPU
fit() throws unless there is exactly one trainer worker; RoleWorkerGroup::call_* throw; no FSDP/ZeRO or grad all-reduce.

Ratio ≈ 1
π_old is recomputed right before the single optimizer step, so the PPO clip rarely bites (pg_clipfrac ≈ 0).

No off-policy correction
rollout_log_probs is diagnostic only; decoupled_ppo.* is parsed but never read.

No entropy
Not computed or regularized (docs/ENTROPY_PLAN.md).

Advantage registry bypassed
compute_advantage calls GRPO directly with a literal 1e-6; adv_estimator: gae parses but has no implementation.

Validation partition
RolloutWorker hard-codes partition "train" (TODO in run_prompt).

Ray C++ constraints
Actors are found by name, not passed as handles (that crashed Ray); positional MSGPACK_DEFINE wire structs must be kept in sync by hand.

Orphan binary
lib/train_grpo_sync has no source in the tree — logs show a synchronous 4-GPU colocated variant.
Stale docs: README.md ("mostly scaffolding"), STATUS.md (no KV cache, MathEquivalence a placeholder) and include/replay_buffer/README.md (FakeTQClient) lag the code.
